questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India was established on _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** April 1, 1935.**__

• **Reserve Bank of India:- **

 
 
• RBI is India’s apex central banking institution.
 
• It was established on April 1, 1935.
 
• It was formed through Legal framework of Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• It was formed on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission.
 
• Initial Paid-up capital was 5 crores.
 
• Initially, it was owned entirely by private shareholders. Following India's independence on 15 August 1947, the RBI was nationalized on 1 January 1949.
 
• The Central Office of the Reserve Bank was initially established in Calcutta but was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937. 
 
• Ownership: Government of India (100%)
 
• **Headquarter: Mumbai, Maharashtra**
 
• The current Governor (as per October 2023) is Shaktikanta Das

questions.question: _________ are an example of public goods and services.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**roads**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Roads**:-

 
 
• **These are thoroughfares for the conveyance of traffic that mostly have an improved surface for use by vehicles (motorized and non-motorized) and pedestrians. **
 
• **It is an example of public goods and services.**
 
• Roads can be classified into a variety of types, including:
 
 
• **Highways**: These are high-speed roads with multiple lanes and limited access. They are typically used for long-distance travel.
 
• **Arterial roads:** These are major roads that connect cities and towns. They typically have multiple lanes and traffic signals.
 
• **Collector roads:** These roads connect arterial roads to local roads. They typically have fewer lanes and lower speed limits.
 
• **Local roads: **These roads provide access to individual homes and businesses. They typically have one lane in each direction and low speed limits.

questions.question: Which of the following states has a bicameral legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Six States have a Legislative Council. They are :
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka.
 
 
 
• Just as Parliament has two Houses, the states can also have a Legislative Council in addition to the Legislative Assembly through Article 169 of the Constitution.
 
• While the Legislative Council is a permanent House like the Rajya Sabha, it cannot be dissolved.
 
• Bicameral literally means 'two-Chamber'. A bicameral parliament is one that contains two separate assemblies that must both agree when new laws are made.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Legislative Council elects its Chairman, who plays the role of presiding officer and Deputy Chairman from amongst its members.
 
• One-third of the members of this House are elected by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• One-third are elected by local bodies like a municipality or other local authorities.
 
• One-twelfth of the members are elected by graduates.

questions.question: During which movement did Chauri-Chaura incident happen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-cooperation movement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Non-cooperation movement:**

 
 
• It was a civil disobedience movement launched in British India in 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• **The movement was based on the principle of non-violent resistance and was aimed at pressurizing the British government to grant India independence.**
 
• The movement involved a boycott of British goods, institutions, and services, as well as the resignation of Indians from government jobs and titles.
 
• **The Chauri Chaura incident happened during the Non-cooperation movement.**
 
 
 
• **Chauri Chaura incident:-**
 
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on February 4, 1922, in the town of Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces (present-day Uttar Pradesh) in British India.
 
• **It was a violent incident between Indian protesters and British police that took place during the Non-cooperation movement.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement: **

 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1942 by the Indian National Congress. **
 
• The movement demanded the immediate withdrawal of the British from India.
 
• The British government responded by cracking down on the movement and arresting thousands of leaders and activists.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Movement: **
 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1917 by Mahatma Gandhi to support the indigo farmers of Champaran district in Bihar. **
 
• The farmers were being forced to grow indigo at low prices and were subjected to various abuses by the indigo planters.
 
• Gandhi's intervention led to the establishment of a commission of inquiry, which recommended several reforms for the benefit of the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement: **
 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1930 by Mahatma Gandhi. **
 
• The movement was aimed at challenging the British Salt Act, which imposed a tax on salt. Gandhi led a march to the sea, where he made salt illegally, in defiance of the law.
 
• The movement spread across India and involved millions of people.

questions.question: As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rupees two crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Consumer Protection Rules, 2021:-**

 
 
• **The Consumer Protection Rules, 2021 were notified by the Central Government on July 22, 2021. **
 
• They were framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which replaced the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.
 
• **As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees.**
 
• The **previous pecuniary jurisdiction of the National Commission was one crore rupees, but it was increased to two crore rupees by the Consumer Protection Rules, 2021**.
 
• This means that consumers can now file complaints with the National Commission for grievances involving goods or services worth more than two crore rupees.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Commission:-**

 
 
• It is the highest consumer forum in India, and it has the power to award compensation, order replacement of goods, and refund of money to consumers.
 
• It can also issue directions to businesses to stop unfair practices.

questions.question: _________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**food deterioration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Food deterioration:-**

__
 
• **It is a natural process that occurs over time in all foods. **
 
• **It is caused by a variety of factors, including:**
 
 
• **Microorganisms**: Bacteria, yeasts, and molds can grow on food and cause it to spoil.
 
• **Enzymes**: Enzymes are naturally occurring proteins that speed up chemical reactions. In food, enzymes can cause food to break down and spoil.
 
• **Oxygen**: Oxygen can cause food to oxidize and become rancid.
 
• **Light**: Light can cause food to discolor and lose nutrients.
 
• **Temperature**: Temperature can affect the rate of food deterioration. Food spoils more quickly at warm temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Food deterioration can cause a variety of problems, including:**
 
 
• **Spoilage**: Spoiled food is unsafe to eat and can cause food poisoning.
 
• **Off-flavors**: Food that is starting to deteriorate may develop off-flavors, such as sourness, bitterness, or staleness.
 
• **Deterioration of textures**: Food that is deteriorating may become slimy, mushy, or tough.
 
• **Discoloration**: Food that is deteriorating may change color, such as browning or fading.
 
• **Loss of nutritional value: **Food that is deteriorating may lose some of its nutrients.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Food processing:-**

 
 
• It can be any method used to turn raw food into food products.
 
• It can involve one or a combination of the following: washing, chopping, pasteurizing, freezing, fermenting, packaging, and more.
 
 
 
• **Food preservation:-**
 
 
• It is the process of treating and handling food to prevent or slow down its spoilage. 
 
 
 
• **Food conservation:-**
 
 
• It is the practice of keeping food fresh and edible for as long as possible.

questions.question: A sudden and constant rainfall, along with violent thunder and lightning is called the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Burst of the monsoon.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Burst of the monsoon:-**

 
 
• **The burst of the monsoon is the sudden onset of the monsoon rains, which typically occurs in June in India. **
 
• **It is characterized by a sudden increase in rainfall and humidity, along with thunderstorms and lightning. **
 
• The burst of the monsoon is a welcome relief from the hot and dry pre-monsoon weather, but it can also bring with it severe weather conditions, such as flooding and landslides.
 
• The burst of the monsoon is caused by a number of factors, including:
 
 
• **The northward movement of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**, a belt of low pressure and high rainfall that encircles the equator.
 
• **The onset of the southwesterly monsoon winds**, which bring moisture from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal to India.
 
• **The heating of the land surface,** which creates instability in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cloudburst Monsoon:-**

 
 
• ** A cloudburst monsoon is a sudden and intense rainfall event that occurs during the monsoon season. **
 
• Cloudbursts can dump large amounts of rain in a short period of time, often over a small area.
 
• This can lead to flash floods, landslides, and other damage.
 
 
 
• **Onset of the monsoon**
 
 
• **The onset of the monsoon is the time when the monsoon winds reach a certain region and begin to bring significant rainfall. **
 
• The monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds that brings rain to many parts of the world, including India.

questions.question: Which of the following does not come from sugarcane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**honey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Honey:-**

 
 
• **It is a sweet, golden liquid produced by bees from the nectar of flowers.**
 
• It is a natural sweetener that has been used by humans for centuries.
 
• Honey is also a good source of antioxidants and other nutrients.
 
• **Honey does not come from sugarcane.**
 
• **Honey is produced by bees from the nectar of flowers. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sugar:-**

 
 
• **It is a refined product made from sugarcane juice. **
 
• The juice is boiled and crystallized, and the molasses is removed.
 
• Sugar is the most processed of the three products, and it is also the sweetest.
 
 
 
• **Khandsari:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of unrefined sugar that is made by boiling sugarcane juice until it thickens and forms crystals. **
 
• The molasses is not removed, so khandsari has a darker color and a more robust flavor than sugar.
 
 
 
• **Molasses:-**
 
 
• **It is a thick, dark syrup that is produced as a byproduct of sugar refining. **
 
• It contains the minerals and vitamins that are removed from sugar during processing.
 
• Molasses has a rich, sweet flavor and is often used in baking and cooking.

• In this role, she represents India's interests and articulates India's position on various UN policies and decisions.
 
• Ruchira Kamboj has received various awards and honors for her work. These include:
 
 
• **Padma Shri**, the fourth highest civilian award of the Government of India (2023)
 
• **Rashtrapati Padak, **the highest civilian award of the Government of India (2015)
 
• **Distinguished Service Award** of the Indian Foreign Service (2012).

• ** Asoke Kumar Mukerji:-**

 
 
• **He is a former Indian diplomat and writer, who teaches diplomacy at the Diplo Foundation.**
 
• He was Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations from April 2013 to December 2015.
 
 
 
• **Syed Akbaruddin:-**
 
 
• **He is a retired Indian diplomat from the 1985 batch of the Indian Foreign Service. **
 
• He served as India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations at New York from January 2016 to April 2020.
 
 
 
• Nirupam Sen:-
 
 
• **He was a Bengali Marxist political leader and former Commerce and Industries minister of the Government of West Bengal during 2001 to 2011. **
 
• He was a senior leader of Communist Party of India (Marxist).
 
• He was a member of the politburo of the party between 2008 and 2015. He was elected to the Member of Legislative Assembly thrice in 1987, 2001 and 2006.
